page: Amazon Web Services c9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 model running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

In multi-core processing and memory bandwidth benchmarks, the c9g.metal-48xl demonstrates top-tier performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests, PassMark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only large block speeds reaching 726.85 GB/sec and write speeds at 339.15 GB/sec. However, single-core CPU performance is moderate, as shown by stress-ng single-core results in the middle 50%.

This bare-metal instance is highly efficient for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high core density and memory bandwidth without requiring GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing. While prompt processing for medium-sized language models is highly efficient at 384.03 tokens/sec, text generation speeds are significantly lower, making it less optimal for real-time LLM text generation.
